item.title: Exploring Fractional Quantum Hall States with Deep Learning: From Abelian to Non-Abelian Phases
item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Xiangyu Ma, Kehuang Chen, Yuntian Gu, Weiluo Ren, Ji Chen, Di Luo, Fengcheng Wu, Xiang Li
arXiv:2610.38533v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Fractional quantum Hall systems host strongly correlated topological phases with potential applications in topological quantum computation, yet identifying their microscopic ground states remains challenging because competing phases are often nearly degenerate and Landau-level mixing is difficult to treat. Here, we introduce a symmetry-adapted neural-network wavefunction that describes Abelian and non-Abelian states while incorporating all Landau levels. The method accurately captures composite-fermion liquids and the emergence of Wigner crystallization at low filling. When the first Landau level is partially filled, finite-size overlaps and entanglement spectra provide evidence consistent with bar2k1k⁺¹-type parton phases at ν=4/3 and 7/5…

👤 Yunhao Fan, Gia-Wei Chern
arXiv:2601.04104v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop point-group equivariant neural networks for learning local mappings used in dynamical simulations of lattice systems. The same network acts on a finite neighborhood around each site, respecting lattice translations through shared parameters. The local configuration is decomposed into features that transform according to irreducible representations of the point group, and hidden features retain this organization throughout the network. Equivariant linear maps and symmetry-allowed tensor products then learn nonlinear spatial correlations while preserving the required transformation laws. item.description:
📚 Machine Learning: Science and Technology
👤 Antonio Guerra, Daniel Uzcategui-Contreras, Aldo Delgado and Esteban S Gómez
Quantum systems governed by time-dependent Hamiltonians pose significant challenges for the accurate computation of their unitary time-evolution operators. In this work, we introduce a deep learning approach based on physics-informed neural networks to estimate these operators over the full time domain, either by predicting the time-evolution operator directly or by predicting an effective Hamiltonian from which that operator is computed. Unitarity is imposed as a constraint in the first case, and holds by construction in the second, where a propagation layer based on the second-order Magnus expansion or Trotterization maps the predicted Hamiltonian to the evolution operator. arXiv:2610.38937v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Friction and wear of diamond are controlled by its surface chemistry, which determines whether covalent bonds form across the sliding interface. First-principles simulations have explored the role of surface orientation and passivation, but are limited to a few hundred atoms and tens of picoseconds. item.title: Convolutional neural network versus persistence for forecasting syndrome rate threshold crossings
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Ashton Reddy
Calibration drift makes the reliability of quantum processors change over time, motivating tools that forecast degradation from data already produced during error correction. We test whether a convolutional neural network (CNN) can predict, from eight cycles of syndrome statistics, whether the next cycle's nonzero-syndrome rate in a simulated three-qubit bit-flip code will exceed a fixed threshold. Fifteen independent drifting-noise trajectories (6,000 cycles) were split by trajectory into training, validation, and test sets, so no cycle was shared between sets. On three held-out trajectories the CNN reached 89.6% accuracy and 98.0% recall for threshold crossings, while a last-cycle persistence baseline reached 91.2% accuracy. Short-horizon crossings are therefore predictable under slow d…

item.title: Optimizing the non-Clifford-count in unitary synthesis using reinforcement learning
item.description:
📚 Machine Learning: Science and Technology
👤 David Kremer, Ali Javadi-Abhari and Priyanka Mukhopadhyay
In this paper we study the potential of using reinforcement learning (RL) in order to synthesize quantum circuits, while optimizing the T-count and CS-count, of unitaries that are exactly implementable by the Clifford+T and Clifford+CS gate sets, respectively. We have designed our RL framework to work with channel representation of unitaries, that enables us to perform matrix operations efficiently, using integers only. We have also incorporated pruning heuristics and a canonicalization of operators, in order to reduce the search complexity. As a result, compared to previous works, we are able to implement significantly larger unitaries, in less time, with much better success rate and improvement factor. Our results for Clifford+T synthesis on two qubit unitaries achieve close-to-optimal…

We developed TileSAM3, a universal droplet segmentation tool built on the Segment Anything Model 3 (SAM3). The proposed models are evaluated on a dataset comprising over 3 million samples from 3,713 PV installations across 33 European countries. We assess convergence speed, forecasting accuracy, transferability across geogra…

item.title: Integrating Density Functional Theory, Machine Learning, and Device Simulation for Perovskite Photovoltaics: A Review
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Sameer Pandey
Metal halide and lead-free double perovskites are promising materials for next-generation photovoltaics. But it is a challenge to navigate their huge compositional space and to simultaneously control long-term stability and non-radiative recombination. This review provides a critical synthesis of the cross-scale computational paradigm that brings together Density Functional Theory (DFT), machine learning (ML) and macroscopic device simulations like SCAPS-1D. We discuss how to transform first-principles atomistic parameters such as band edge alignments, dielectric constants and effective masses into meaningful device parameters without physical oversimplification. item.title: Machine learning helps track semiconductor defects under more realistic temperature conditions
item.description:
📚 Physics News
All materials contain inherent defects. These are not always harmful, since they can be used to engineer and introduce certain properties into a material. However, it is crucial to understand how they function and how they affect the material's properties.

arXiv:2610.37754v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Altermagnets are collinear magnets with zero net magnetization and spin-split electronic bands. item.title: Quantum skyrmions outlast entanglement, hinting at more resilient networks
item.description:
📚 Physics News
Quantum networks could one day connect quantum computers into more powerful systems and enable new forms of secure communication. But a fundamental obstacle stands in the way: Quantum information is extraordinarily fragile, and the entanglement between particles of light on which such networks would depend is easily disrupted.

Tuning a laser–wakefield accelerator to a desired electron energy spectrum is normally done by scanning the machine one setting at a time, which consumes scarce beam time and expert attention. item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Oumaïma Bounhar, Thomas Chêne, Ghaya Rekaya-Ben Othman, Oussama Damen
arXiv:2610.39827v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RIS) are a promising solution for improving millimeter-wave (mmWave) communications by controlling signal propagation. Yet, selecting the optimal RIS configuration remains challenging due to the high-dimensional search space and signaling overhead. We propose a Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) framework for blind passive beamforming, where a Deep Q-Learning (DQL) agent learns an adaptive policy to select near-optimal RIS configurations while sounding only few codewords, without channel state information. Results show that our approach outperforms Q-Learning (QL) and conventional baselines in convergence, performance, and overhead reduction.
